The study highlights the potential of multiprobe grid algorithms in scenarios with frequent data rebuilds or high-dimensional data where indexing efficiency and dimensional robustness are critical. Furthermore, since recent research connects self-attention mechanisms to ANN operations, understanding the scaling behavior of ANN algorithms could inform the design of more efficient transformer architectures. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration.

item.title: Survey reviews generative AI and federated learning techniques for intrusion detection systems, covering model types, applications, and open challenges in privacy-sensitive network environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This survey examines the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and federated learning (FL) techniques in Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), which are critical for monitoring network traffic and detecting malicious activities across various environments such as IoT and enterprise networks. It highlights the challenges in developing effective IDS models, including evolving attack behaviors, limited datasets, and privacy constraints, and explores how generative AI supports tasks like anomaly detection and synthetic data generation, while FL enables collaborative training without sharing sensitive data. The review categorizes IDS research directions and generative AI applications by model types, including autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks, diffusion models, and Large Language Models. It also discusses the integration of generative AI with FL-based IDS and identifies open challenges such as ensuring synthetic data quality, managing adversarial risks, handling non-independent client data distributions, and developing domain-specific models for network security.

item.title: Researchers use sparse autoencoders to interpret and causally steer neural quantum states, revealing unsupervised features linked to physical observables without affecting variational energy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a method using sparse autoencoders to analyze the internal activations of Neural Quantum States (NQS), a powerful class of variational models for quantum many-body wavefunctions. Their approach uncovers unsupervised features within NQS that strongly correlate with physical observables like order parameters and magnetization, despite these observables not being explicitly targeted during training. By intervening on individual features post-training, they demonstrated causal control over corresponding physical observables without significantly affecting the variational energy. This work reveals that NQS encode rich, interpretable internal representations beyond mere functional approximation, providing new tools for diagnosing and steering these models. The findings offer a foundation for mechanistic interpretability in quantum state modeling, potentially leading to more transparent and reliable applications of NQS in quantum physics research.

item.title: Researchers propose TurnNat, a likelihood-based framework for automatic evaluation of turn-taking naturalness in dyadic spoken dialogue, validated by human judgments on perturbed dialogue benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TurnNat, a new likelihood-based framework designed to automatically evaluate the naturalness of turn-taking in two-speaker spoken dialogues. This approach uses a causal prediction model trained on natural conversations to estimate future voice activity and measures timing atypicality through negative log-likelihood scores. TurnNat aggregates these scores over turn-taking boundary units to produce a dialogue-level naturalness score, providing a unified method to assess various timing irregularities. To validate TurnNat, the researchers created a benchmark consisting of paired natural and perturbed dialogue clips, which were also evaluated by human judges. Experimental results demonstrate that TurnNat effectively identifies unnatural turn-taking patterns across different types of timing failures, offering a promising tool for improving full-duplex spoken dialogue systems.

item.title: Researchers propose AI system using multi-modal data to assess railway crossing safety with results aligning to Federal Railroad Administration scores and expert opinion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an AI system that assesses the safety of railway crossings by analyzing multi-modal data, including images and structured accident reports. The system aims to provide safety scores that align with expert evaluations and the Federal Railroad Administration's (FRA) standards. Their proof-of-concept pipeline successfully identifies high-risk and low-risk crossings with a macro F1 score of 0.757 and estimates FRA-based safety scores with notable accuracy. The approach integrates visual cues from images with historical accident data to improve safety assessments. Using a fine-tuned visual-language model, the system achieves a root mean square error of 0.078 and a correlation of 0.492 with FRA scores, demonstrating its potential to support expert decision-making in railway crossing safety analysis.

item.title: Researchers compare discrete, continuous, and hybrid numeric encoding strategies for transformers in electronic health records, finding hybrid token-based approaches offer robust, practical defaults for clinical tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have conducted a systematic comparison of discrete, continuous, and hybrid numeric encoding strategies for transformer models processing electronic health record (EHR) data. Their study evaluates these approaches using synthetic arithmetic tasks embedded in real-world EHR data and clinical prediction tasks, revealing trade-offs between numeric precision, optimization stability, and architectural flexibility. They found that methods explicitly modeling value-concept interactions excel in precision-sensitive tasks when architectural constraints allow, while hybrid token-based approaches that bin numeric values before projection offer a robust and broadly applicable alternative. The research shows that the optimal number of bins in hybrid approaches follows a power-law relationship with dataset size. Across various tasks, models tend to perform reliable "good enough" numeric computations rather than exact arithmetic, and the clinical benefits of incorporating laboratory values vary depending on the task. These findings suggest that prioritizing robustness and deployability over maximal numeric precision makes hybrid token-based encoding a practical default for clinical transformer applications.

item.title: arXiv:2607.01395 proposes methods to improve generic object tracking models by enhancing target discrimination, adaptation, and geometric reasoning to approach human-level visual perception [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The paper arXiv:2607.01395 addresses the challenge of improving generic object tracking models to better emulate human visual perception. It proposes methods to enhance target discrimination, robust adaptation, and geometric reasoning, aiming to maintain continuous and coherent tracking of objects despite variations in appearance, environment, and unforeseen changes. This work seeks to bridge the gap between machine and human visual tracking capabilities by enabling models to better handle complex scene dynamics and unpredictable real-world conditions. The study highlights the limitations of current tracking systems, which often struggle with severe target deformation, distractors, environmental changes, and unseen object categories. By integrating prior knowledge, spatial geometry, and semantic context, the proposed approaches aim to improve the generalization and online adaptation of tracking models, moving closer to human-level perceptual intelligence in visual object tracking tasks.

item.title: Researchers develop NeuroBridge, a multi-task MRI framework achieving up to 88% accuracy in Alzheimer's and dementia diagnosis across ADNI and OASIS cohorts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed NeuroBridge, a multi-task MRI analysis framework designed to improve the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and related dementias. By integrating self-supervised MRI pretraining with tasks such as hippocampal segmentation and atrophy classification, NeuroBridge achieved up to 88% accuracy in distinguishing AD from cognitively normal controls across the ADNI and OASIS cohorts. The framework also showed strong performance in mixed-diagnosis settings and demonstrated effective cross-cohort generalization. NeuroBridge's approach combines multiple diagnostic objectives with gated fusion fine-tuning, enabling more robust detection of subtle and heterogeneous structural brain changes associated with neurodegenerative diseases. The system's probability-based analysis supports opportunistic screening, potentially enhancing early detection efforts. This multi-task learning framework offers a scalable and clinically guided tool that surpasses traditional single-task MRI diagnostic methods for dementia assessment.

item.title: Researchers present SpinGTP using Spin-Weighted Spherical Harmonics to enable complete and scalable E(3)-equivariant networks for 3D atomistic modeling, improving expressivity and efficiency over prior methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SpinGTP, a novel approach that uses Spin-Weighted Spherical Harmonics to enhance E(3)-equivariant networks for 3D atomistic modeling. This method addresses the limitations of previous tensor product techniques by capturing antisymmetric interactions while maintaining computational efficiency, enabling more complete and scalable modeling of complex 3D systems. SpinGTP generalizes from scalar functions to a more expressive equivariant basis, naturally incorporating parity-odd components and overcoming the expressivity gaps of the Gaunt Tensor Product. Evaluations on benchmarks such as Tetris, 3BPA, SPICE-MACE-OFF, and OC20 demonstrate that SpinGTP achieves accuracy comparable to the full Clebsch-Gordan Tensor Product, with improved performance in modeling chiral materials and non-centrosymmetric geometries. This advancement offers a mathematically rigorous and scalable framework for high-order equivariance in large-scale 3D atomistic simulations, potentially benefiting research in materials science and molecular modeling by enabling more accurate and efficient computational analyses.

item.title: GPUAlert launches a zero-instrumentation process-boundary monitor that diagnoses GPU training-job failures with classified causes and durable logs, achieving 0.997 macro-F1 on 12 hardware-reproduced failure classes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: GPUAlert is a command-line tool designed to monitor GPU training jobs without requiring any changes to the training commands. It provides timely, structured notifications upon job completion, including classified failure causes, durable logs, and output artifacts, addressing the common issue of delayed failure detection in large production clusters. The tool achieves high accuracy in diagnosing failures, with a macro-F1 score of 0.997 on twelve hardware-reproduced failure classes, significantly outperforming traditional methods like keyword matching and exit-code inspection. The system is built around three key reliability features: a pre-launch log guarantee that secures log storage before a process can crash, notifier isolation ensuring the wrapper's exit code reflects the child process's status regardless of email success, and a controlled artifact size policy that prevents silent data loss. GPUAlert introduces minimal overhead, approximately 3 milliseconds per job, and maintains consistent exit codes even when email notifications fail. The developers have also released a labeled dataset of 474 GPU training logs across 15 failure categories and an evaluation framework to support further research and development in this area.

item.title: Researchers introduce MultAttnAttrib, a training-free method for multimodal attribution in long document QA, outperforming prompting approaches and matching GPT 5.4 with lower latency [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MultAttnAttrib, a training-free method for generating multimodal attributions in long document question answering. This approach uses a model's prefill pass, selected attention heads, and calibrated thresholds to identify source evidence within documents, improving accuracy and efficiency. The team also introduced MultAttrEval, the first benchmark dataset with fine-grained, ground-truth attributions for multimodal long-form documents. Experimental results demonstrate that MultAttnAttrib outperforms various attribution methods, including strong prompting-based approaches, and matches the performance of advanced models like GPT 5.4. Additionally, it achieves these results with significantly lower latency, producing attributions up to seven times faster than prompting on the same base model.

item.title: Researchers introduce ISOSCI benchmark to separate reasoning from knowledge retrieval in LLMs, finding 91.3% of reasoning gains depend on domain knowledge across five model pairs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ISOSCI, a benchmark designed to distinguish reasoning ability from domain knowledge retrieval in large language models (LLMs). ISOSCI uses pairs of science problems with identical logical structures but different domain-specific knowledge requirements, allowing for precise measurement of reasoning gains. Analysis across five model pairs from four families revealed that 91.3% of reasoning improvements depend on domain knowledge rather than on reasoning structure alone, challenging the belief that chain-of-thought reasoning significantly enhances scientific problem-solving accuracy. The study found that enabling reasoning modes in highly capable models yields less than a 5 percentage point accuracy improvement across various domains. Additionally, a reasoning-specialized model that performed well on one benchmark underperformed on ISOSCI, highlighting how benchmark selection influences conclusions about reasoning effectiveness. The ISOSCI dataset has been made publicly available for further research and evaluation.

item.title: Researchers introduce Ember, a lightweight optimizer for language model embeddings and LM-heads that reduces VRAM usage and improves training efficiency, with open-source distributed implementation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Ember, a lightweight optimizer designed specifically for language model embeddings and LM-head matrices. Ember significantly reduces VRAM usage by requiring only O(V + D) memory compared to the traditional Adam optimizer's O(2VD), and eliminates the need to shard token table optimizer states. This innovation improves training efficiency across supervised finetuning, reinforcement learning, and pretraining while maintaining a minimal optimizer state footprint. The team demonstrated that Ember scales effectively with batch size and model parameters, and revealed that token optimization trajectories can be approximated by a simple one-dimensional ray, challenging the common view of neural network parameter landscapes as highly nonconvex. They also provide insights into the limited range of optimizers suitable for Transformer training. The researchers have open-sourced their distributed Ember implementation, which integrates smoothly with existing ZeRO and FSDP frameworks to facilitate further research.

item.title: Researchers present Grounded Optimization, a five-layer framework reducing hallucinations in LLM-based resume rewriting by up to 95%, releasing taxonomy and evaluation data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Grounded Optimization, a five-layer framework designed to significantly reduce hallucinations in large language model (LLM)-based resume rewriting, achieving up to a 95% decrease in errors. This framework addresses specific hallucination types such as anachronistic technology insertion, cross-domain terminology contamination, structural changes, and fabricated content by combining temporal context validation, contamination detection, structural enforcement, prompt-level grounding, and an evaluator agent. In experiments involving multiple LLMs, temperature settings, and configurations on synthetic resumes from various industries, the framework reduced detected hallucinations from an average of 2.48-5.36 per resume to as low as 0.04-0.24. Prompt-level grounding alone eliminated hallucinations at low temperatures with capable models, while the full layered approach was necessary for more challenging conditions. The researchers have also released a taxonomy of contamination types, evaluation code, and raw data to support further study and application.

item.title: Researchers propose FADE, a self-adapting advantage function for reinforcement learning that accelerates LLM reasoning training and improves accuracy-diversity trade-offs on LiveCodeBench and AIME [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced FADE (Focal Advantage with Dynamic Entropy), a self-adapting advantage function designed to enhance reinforcement learning (RL) for large language model (LLM) reasoning. FADE dynamically adjusts gradient weights during training to balance exploration and exploitation, addressing issues of training instability and diversity collapse common in RL post-training. This approach accelerates training, reaching peak performance significantly earlier than static baselines, and improves the trade-off between accuracy and diversity on benchmarks like LiveCodeBench and AIME. The study presents a unifying framework that decomposes advantage functions along two axes-sign and difficulty-highlighting how imbalanced updates can harm entropy or weight geometry and how focusing on harder problems sharpens learning signals but requires more samples. FADE leverages this insight to adaptively schedule gradient weights based on training dynamics, optimizing learning efficiency and effectiveness across different model scales. By achieving faster convergence and superior accuracy-diversity balance, FADE offers a promising advancement for RL in LLM training, potentially influencing future methods for improving reasoning capabilities in AI systems.

item.title: Researchers introduce Evolutionary Feature Engineering framework using LLM-based evolution to improve preprocessing and accuracy in time-series forecasting and tabular prediction [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Evolutionary Feature Engineering (EFE), a framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to evolve preprocessing transformations for structured data, enhancing machine learning pipelines. EFE represents these transformations as Python programs with a standardized interface, allowing seamless integration and refinement based on dataset context and validation performance. The framework is applied in two domains: time-series forecasting and tabular prediction, demonstrating improvements in accuracy and interpretability. In time-series forecasting, EFE-Time generates dataset-specific normalizations that reduce forecasting errors by 3% on average and up to 19% on certain datasets, such as COVID-Deaths, even when used with advanced models like Chronos-2. For tabular data, EFE-Tab evolves compact, interpretable feature sets that improve or match existing LLM-based methods, particularly benefiting classical decision tree models by maintaining accuracy while enhancing interpretability. Overall, EFE shows that LLM-driven evolutionary methods can effectively optimize feature engineering for structured data tasks.

item.title: Researchers introduce X-LogSMask, a multi-head logarithmic structural mask that integrates graph topology into Transformer attention, achieving state-of-the-art results on 13 of 20 graph learning benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed X-LogSMask, a multi-head logarithmic structural mask that integrates graph topology directly into Transformer attention mechanisms. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional Transformers in handling graph-structured data by using a logarithmic transform to create a topology-aware gating signal, which suppresses unsupported node interactions while preserving feature-dependent attention. By assigning different powers of the normalized adjacency matrix to various attention heads, X-LogSMask enables multi-hop information propagation within a single layer and defines a structural radius for each head. The study demonstrates that standard Transformer encoders can be viewed as one-step message passing on complete graphs, positioning X-LogSMask as a topology-constrained alternative to unrestricted self-attention. Tested across 20 node-, edge-, and graph-level benchmarks, Transformers equipped with X-LogSMask achieved state-of-the-art results on 13 datasets and maintained competitive performance even in a lightweight one-layer configuration. These findings suggest that simple, interpretable structural masks can enhance self-attention for graph learning without altering the Transformer architecture.

item.title: Researchers propose DiPS, a Q-learning framework for dynamic dialogue policy selection to improve persuasion success in high-stakes fire-rescue evacuation scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed DiPS, a Q-learning framework designed to improve persuasion success in high-stakes fire-rescue evacuation scenarios by dynamically selecting dialogue policies tailored to individual residents. This approach addresses the limitations of large language models (LLMs) that often struggle with persuasion due to the need for personalized strategies based on people's unique personalities and concerns. DiPS trains a critic to maximize evacuation success by choosing appropriate persuasion strategies at each conversational turn, adapting to the resident's recent responses. The framework was evaluated against several baselines in both simulated environments and real human interactions, demonstrating higher evacuation success rates compared to zero-shot LLMs and generic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods. This dynamic policy selection represents a significant advancement in applying AI to critical communication tasks where personalized persuasion is essential for safety outcomes.

item.title: Researchers present ADVENT, an LLM-driven automatic predicate invention method for Inductive Logic Programming that improves success rates to 80% with formal verification and enables cross-task knowledge reuse [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ADVENT, a novel method that uses large language models (LLMs) to automate predicate invention in Inductive Logic Programming (ILP), significantly improving success rates to 80% through formal verification. ADVENT combines LLM-based abductive generation with Prolog deductive verification in an iterative process, enabling the creation of meaningful auxiliary predicates that extend the hypothesis space. This approach also supports cross-task knowledge reuse by accumulating invented predicates and learned rules in a shared knowledge pool. Testing ADVENT on nine poker-hand concepts across seven different LLMs demonstrated that LLM-driven predicate invention alone achieved a 58% success rate where traditional ILP methods failed entirely, with formal verification boosting this to 80%. The knowledge pool further enhanced performance by up to 31 percentage points, while producing human-interpretable rules. These findings suggest that ADVENT offers a promising direction for automating predicate invention and facilitating knowledge transfer across tasks in ILP.

item.title: Researchers present MKGR, a multimodal knowledge-graph and sequence-based framework for cold-start protein-protein interaction prediction, outperforming baselines on benchmark datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MKGR, a multimodal framework designed to improve protein-protein interaction (PPI) prediction, especially in cold-start scenarios where proteins lack prior interaction data. MKGR integrates region-aware protein sequence encoding with four biomedical knowledge graphs covering protein-drug, protein-disease, protein-miRNA, and protein-lncRNA associations. This approach combines sequence context and graph-based embeddings, using a bridge reconstruction objective and a gating module to effectively merge information for each protein pair. Tests on two benchmark datasets under novel-old and novel-novel cold-start conditions demonstrate that MKGR consistently outperforms existing sequence, network, and knowledge-graph methods across multiple evaluation metrics, including accuracy, F1 score, AUC, AUPR, and MCC. This advancement offers a promising tool for functional genomics, disease mechanism research, and drug development by addressing challenges in predicting interactions involving previously unobserved proteins.

item.title: Researchers introduce Explainability Stability Index to evaluate adversarial robustness and explanation stability in Random Forest and XGBoost cybersecurity classifiers across four tabular datasets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Explainability Stability Index (ESI) to assess both adversarial robustness and the stability of SHAP-based explanations in cybersecurity classifiers using Random Forest and XGBoost models across four tabular datasets. Their study evaluates five adversarial attacks, including black-box methods suited for non-differentiable tree models, revealing that prediction robustness and explanation stability are distinct and both require measurement. Notably, gradient-based black-box attacks showed misleading robustness against XGBoost, while score-based attacks exposed genuine vulnerabilities, with significant attribution drift observed despite apparent prediction stability. The research extends previous work on multilayer perceptrons by applying the analysis to tree ensemble models and introduces a two-axis framework based on gradient dependence and query efficiency to explain attack effectiveness. This framework provides practical guidance for evaluating tree-based classifiers in cybersecurity. Additionally, the study investigates anomalies in attack behavior related to data normalization, offering deeper insights into adversarial impacts on model explanations and predictions.

item.title: Researchers formulate model merging as probabilistic inference using heavy-tailed product-of-experts to improve multi-task fine-tuning without additional data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new approach to model merging that combines single-task solutions into a multi-task model without requiring additional fine-tuning data. Their method frames model merging as probabilistic inference using a product-of-experts (PoE) framework, where each task-specific model acts as an energy-based expert. This approach addresses limitations of previous methods that relied on geometric assumptions and Gaussian distributions, which often did not fit the observed heavy-tailed residuals between merged and task-specific models. The team introduced a heavy-tailed PoE design based on Cauchy distributions to better capture these residuals, resulting in a provably convergent inference process. Experiments across various tasks and architectures demonstrated significant improvements over existing state-of-the-art model merging techniques. The researchers have made their code publicly available to support further exploration and application of their method.

item.title: Researchers develop offline checkpoint selection method using Composite Reward Observability Fraction to predict closed-loop performance of latent world models in LunarLander with non-Markovian rewards [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a method to predict the closed-loop performance of latent world models using offline checkpoint selection, focusing on the LunarLander environment with non-Markovian rewards. They introduced the Composite Reward Observability Fraction (CROF), a score combining the Reward Observability Fraction (ROF) with structural regularizers, to select the best model checkpoints without relying on traditional validation metrics that can be misleading. This approach enables more accurate prediction of model performance in control tasks. The team trained a Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM) on Gymnasium's LunarLander v3 and used the Cross-Entropy Method Model Predictive Control (CEM-MPC) return as a benchmark for closed-loop quality. By evaluating 40 metrics, they identified ROF as the strongest predictor of performance and enhanced it with additional regularizers to form CROF. Models selected by CROF outperformed model-free baselines significantly, achieving higher returns with substantially fewer real-environment interactions. This method not only improves checkpoint selection for model-based reinforcement learning but also supports the development of efficient policies with reduced training data. The researchers have made their code and data publicly available, facilitating further exploration and application of their approach in similar control and reinforcement learning problems.

item.title: Researchers propose LF-IBIS algorithm for full Bayesian reinforcement learning without explicit likelihoods, enabling online belief updates and policy uncertainty quantification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced LF-IBIS, a new algorithm for Bayesian Reinforcement Learning (BRL) that operates without requiring explicit likelihood functions, which are often unavailable or intractable in real-world environments. LF-IBIS combines Approximate Bayesian Computation with Iterated Batch Importance Sampling to enable online belief updates and full Bayesian inference over environment parameters and optimal policies. This approach allows for quantifying policy uncertainty, aiding in the exploration-exploitation trade-off in sequential decision-making tasks. The method was validated through simulation studies in response-adaptive randomization for clinical trials, where closed-form posteriors were available for comparison. Additional experiments demonstrated LF-IBIS's capability to update policies online even when posterior distributions lack closed forms, highlighting its potential for practical applications where traditional BRL methods are limited by the absence of explicit likelihoods.

item.title: Researchers propose a unified framework for decentralized stochastic subgradient methods with communication compression, establishing global convergence for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization problems
item.description: Researchers have developed a unified framework for decentralized stochastic subgradient methods that incorporate communication compression, addressing nonsmooth and nonconvex optimization problems. This framework integrates various methods using unbiased and contractive compression with error compensation, and establishes global convergence even when objective functions lack Clarke regularity. The approach connects consensus-error and averaged iterates to continuous-time differential inclusions to prove convergence. Building on this framework, the team introduced several new compression-based methods, including those employing sign-based regularization and gradient-tracking momentum. Preliminary numerical experiments support the theoretical findings and demonstrate the trade-off between communication efficiency and accuracy in these methods.

item.title: Researchers propose EPnG, an adaptive prune-and-grow framework for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Mixture-of-Experts models, outperforming LoRA while updating under 1% of parameters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced EPnG, an adaptive prune-and-grow framework designed to improve parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. EPnG reallocates fine-tuning capacity by pruning under-utilized experts and expanding important ones based on router gate probabilities, all while maintaining a fixed parameter budget. This approach outperforms existing methods like LoRA, achieving comparable results to full fine-tuning while updating less than 1% of parameters. EPnG was tested on OLMoE and Qwen1.5-MoE models, consistently delivering better performance than LoRA under the same parameter constraints. By aligning fine-tuning strategies with MoE routing dynamics, EPnG offers a more effective and scalable solution for adapting large MoE models efficiently.

item.title: Researchers develop hybrid CNN+LSTM+Attention model using single-channel EEG to assess cognitive load in online learning videos, achieving up to 78.5% accuracy in within-subject tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a hybrid deep learning model combining CNN, LSTM, and attention mechanisms to assess cognitive load during online learning using data from a single-channel, consumer-grade EEG device. The model, tested on a dataset of nine learners, achieved up to 78.5% accuracy in distinguishing between easy and difficult educational video content within subjects, outperforming traditional feature-based classifiers. The study emphasizes caution due to the small sample size and advocates for subject-independent evaluation as a standard for future research. The approach integrates raw EEG waveforms with band-power features and employs regularization techniques to maintain stable validation accuracy. The researchers provide an open, reproducible evaluation pipeline and a notebook-based tool that records EEG data, performs inference, and visualizes cognitive load as a heatmap over video timelines. This tool aims to assist educators in identifying challenging segments in online learning materials, framing the work as a feasibility study rather than a ready-to-deploy system.

item.title: Researchers introduce Expander Sparse Autoencoders with parameter-efficient dictionaries that reduce decoder values by up to 293× while retaining 84% fidelity on large language model activations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Expander Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), a new approach that significantly reduces the number of learned decoder parameters needed to represent neural network activations. By using a left-regular expander mask to enforce sparsity in the decoder and encoder, Expander SAEs achieve up to 293 times fewer decoder values while maintaining 84% of the fidelity compared to dense decoders on large language model activations. This method improves storage efficiency and computational cost without compromising much on performance. The study tested Expander SAEs on various models including Pythia, Qwen, and Llama, demonstrating a consistent tradeoff between storage and fidelity as the sparsity parameter varies. The improvements stem from the sparse and diverse structure of the decoder rather than simply reducing parameter count. Theoretical analysis also shows conditions under which the sparse codes can be exactly recovered, supporting the practical effectiveness of this approach. These findings suggest that Expander SAEs offer a promising direction for mechanistic interpretability and efficient representation in large neural networks, potentially enabling more scalable and interpretable models with reduced resource demands.

item.title: Researchers present Decomposer, a framework that converts symbolic MIDI music into executable Strudel programs using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve reconstruction and code readability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Decomposer, a framework that converts symbolic MIDI music into executable programs written in Strudel, a music programming language. This approach addresses the challenge of recovering high-level musical instructions from performances by translating MIDI inputs into readable and editable code that can faithfully reconstruct the original music when executed. Decomposer uses a two-stage training process involving supervised fine-tuning on a synthetic dataset and reinforcement learning to optimize both reconstruction accuracy and code readability. The framework tackles the scarcity of paired MIDI and Strudel code data by creating Strudel-Synth, a synthetic corpus for initial training, and then refines the model using unpaired MIDI data with reinforcement learning. Evaluations on synthetic and real-world MIDI benchmarks demonstrate that Decomposer outperforms existing closed-source large language models in MIDI reconstruction fidelity while generating more readable and diverse code compared to heuristic converters.

item.title: Researchers evaluate cluster-based semantic chunking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation on academic theses and find it does not outperform simpler chunking methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated whether cluster-based semantic chunking enhances retrieval and answer quality in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems compared to fixed-size and recursive chunking methods. The study focused on long, structured academic theses and used the Retrieval Augmented Generation Assessment (RAGAs) framework to measure performance. Results showed that cluster-based chunking did not outperform simpler chunking strategies under the tested conditions. The evaluation revealed variability in performance between fixed and document-specific questions, likely influenced by document formatting and preprocessing. Additionally, the faithfulness metric based on RAGAs demonstrated limited reliability in this context, suggesting challenges in assessing answer quality for complex academic texts using current methods.

item.title: Researchers introduce Rank-Then-Act, a reward-free control framework using vision-language models and correlation-based reinforcement learning for video demonstration tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Rank-Then-Act (RTA), a novel framework that enables learning control policies from expert video demonstrations without relying on environment rewards. RTA uses a Vision-Language Model trained offline to score progress based on the temporal order of shuffled video frames, emphasizing visual semantics over time cues. Instead of using this scorer as a direct reward, the method employs a correlation-based reward function that measures the Spearman rank correlation between predicted progress and actual frame order, providing a stable and scale-invariant learning signal. The framework was tested on both discrete and continuous control tasks, including PyBoy games and robotic environments like MetaWorld. RTA consistently matched or outperformed existing video-based reward learning approaches and demonstrated effective transferability across different tasks using a single pretrained progress scorer. This approach suggests that leveraging correlation-structured supervision from video-derived ordinal signals can serve as a scalable alternative to traditional reward design in reinforcement learning.

item.title: Researchers propose SABER, a semantic-aligned brain network analysis framework using multi-scale hypergraphs to integrate LLM-derived semantics for improved brain disease diagnosis on ABIDE and ADHD-200 datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SABER, a novel brain network analysis framework that integrates semantic information derived from large language models (LLMs) to enhance brain disease diagnosis. This approach incorporates region-of-interest (ROI) level semantics through global self-attention to enrich brain network representations and constructs multi-scale hypergraphs to capture complex functional interactions. A decision-level semantic alignment mechanism further allows patient-specific textual embeddings to directly influence predictions without altering the underlying network structure. Tests on public datasets, including ABIDE and ADHD-200, show that SABER achieves state-of-the-art diagnostic performance with improved stability and interpretability, especially in scenarios with limited sample sizes. This framework addresses limitations of previous methods that treated LLM semantics only as auxiliary inputs, enabling a more integrated and robust use of semantic knowledge in brain disease classification.

item.title: Researchers propose population-based multi-objective training for discriminators in semi-supervised GANs, improving classification accuracy and training stability on MNIST with limited labels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a population-based evolutionary training method for semi-supervised generative adversarial networks (SSL-GANs) that treats discriminator learning as a multi-objective optimization problem. This approach maintains a population of discriminators ranked by Pareto dominance, allowing the exploration of trade-offs between classification accuracy and real/fake discrimination, rather than combining these objectives into a single loss function. The method aims to enhance both the classifier accuracy and the quality of generated samples in SSL-GANs. Experiments on the MNIST dataset with limited labeled data demonstrate that this multi-objective strategy improves training stability and robustness compared to existing SSL-GAN baselines. Among the variants tested, an elitist strategy consistently achieved the highest classification accuracy, highlighting the benefits of maintaining diverse discriminator populations during training.

item.title: Researchers present TUDUM, a Turkish-thinking reasoning pipeline for Qwen3.5-27B using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning on 15,991 Turkish examples with mixed benchmark results [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TUDUM, a pipeline designed to adapt the Qwen3.5-27B language model for Turkish reasoning tasks. Unlike models that translate Turkish prompts into English for internal processing, TUDUM aims to maintain explicit reasoning in Turkish by training the model to generate Turkish-language reasoning traces. The approach involves supervised fine-tuning on nearly 16,000 Turkish reasoning examples followed by reinforcement learning in a Turkish mathematics environment, resulting in mixed performance outcomes. The supervised fine-tuning phase made the model's reasoning more concise and consistently Turkish but led to a decrease in benchmark accuracy. Subsequent reinforcement learning partially restored mathematical performance on some tests but did not improve all benchmarks or surpass the original model's overall average. The researchers present TUDUM as a transparent pipeline and evaluation framework for Turkish reasoning rather than a state-of-the-art solution. The step-50 model from this project has been made publicly available.

item.title: Researchers release AIriskEval-edu-db2 dataset with 1,639 K-12 educational explanations and annotations for training LLM auditors on pedagogical risk assessment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced AIriskEval-edu-db2, a dataset designed to train and evaluate large language model (LLM) auditors for assessing pedagogical risks in K-12 educational content. The dataset includes 1,639 explanations from 170 ScienceQA questions across science, language arts, and social sciences, featuring both human-written and LLM-generated explanations that simulate various pedagogical risk profiles. It incorporates a detailed risk rubric covering factual accuracy, depth, relevance, appropriateness for students, and ideological bias, along with 785 explanations annotated for explainability and risk localization validated by expert teachers. The team conducted validation experiments comparing state-of-the-art proprietary models with a lightweight local Llama 3.1 8B model to assess their performance in detecting pedagogical risks and providing explainability. Results suggest that fine-tuning on AIriskEval-edu-db2 enables locally deployable models to approach or surpass more powerful models while maintaining privacy, offering a promising approach for educational auditing and assessment tasks.

item.title: Researchers introduce Conditional Co-Ablation to recover self-repair backups in transformer circuits, improving backup-head recovery on GPT-2-small and enabling repair-aware pruning across models from 124M to 7B parameters [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Conditional Co-Ablation (CoAx), a new method to identify and recover backup components in transformer models that self-repair when primary components are removed. This approach improves the detection of backup units by measuring how the effect of ablating remaining units changes after removing a primary set, revealing interactions missed by traditional single-unit scoring. Applied to GPT-2-small and other models ranging from 124 million to 7 billion parameters, CoAx significantly enhances backup-head recovery and supports repair-aware pruning and capability knockout.

item.title: Researchers analyze three LLMs' responses to science skepticism across climate, vaccines, and evolution, finding varied robustness patterns that do not indicate sycophantic retreat but differ by model and domain [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated three open instruction-tuned large language models (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B) on their responses to skepticism about established scientific consensus in climate change, vaccines, and evolution. Contrary to concerns that these models might sycophantically retreat from consensus when faced with doubt, the study found distinct response patterns: Llama increased consensus assertion, Qwen softened its tone while maintaining its stance, and Mistral often did not respond. These behaviors were linked to differences in how the models represent skepticism signals internally. The study combined behavioral analysis with techniques like linear probing and activation patching to understand the models' internal representations. It revealed that robustness to skepticism varies by model and domain, with some models showing weakened rebuttals in critical areas like vaccines under skeptical pressure. The authors propose a taxonomy distinguishing active from accidental robustness and caution that behavioral responses alone cannot determine whether a model truly understands skepticism or simply fails to detect it.

item.title: Researchers benchmark 16 vision-language models on medical image quality assessment across seven corruption types and five severity levels, finding pixelation and metadata bias reduce reliability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated 16 vision-language models (VLMs) for medical image quality assessment (MIQA) using the MediMeta-C dataset, testing across seven types of image corruption and five severity levels. They found that pixelation significantly reduced model performance, while brightness changes had minimal impact. The study also revealed that textual metadata, such as institutional prestige and equipment age, influenced model scores, indicating potential biases. The analysis showed that pixelation, often used to protect patient privacy, compromises the reliability of VLMs in assessing image quality, highlighting a trade-off between privacy and diagnostic accuracy. Additionally, the sensitivity of models to contextual metadata suggests limited objectivity and raises concerns about privacy and bias in automated medical image evaluation. These findings underscore the need for balancing privacy protection with objective quality assessment before deploying VLMs in clinical settings.

item.title: Study compares nine lightweight CNNs on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet, finding newer models offer selective gains in accuracy and efficiency under resource constraints [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study evaluates nine lightweight convolutional neural networks (CNNs) across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet datasets to assess their predictive accuracy and deployment efficiency under resource constraints. The research compares models on metrics including top-1 accuracy, parameter count, computational cost, latency, and memory usage, revealing that newer CNN architectures offer selective improvements rather than consistent gains across all measures. EfficientNetV2-S achieved the highest accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, while RepViT-M1.0 led on Tiny ImageNet, but EfficientNet-B0 demonstrated a strong balance of accuracy and efficiency, appearing on all evaluated Pareto frontiers as a competitive intermediate option. The study also highlights that MobileNetV3-Small is the fastest and most efficient in terms of computational cost, outperforming MobileNetV4-Conv-S in accuracy despite lower resource use. SqueezeNet1.1, while having the fewest parameters and lowest memory allocation, showed substantially weaker accuracy. The findings emphasize that computational metrics like GMACs do not reliably predict inference latency across different hardware, underscoring the complexity of evaluating model performance in practical deployment scenarios.

item.title: Researchers introduce OpenSafeIntent benchmark to evaluate AI model safety across benign, dual-use, and malicious prompt variants, revealing calibration failures and brittleness in intent-sensitive completions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced OpenSafeIntent, a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI model safety by testing how models respond to prompts with varying intents-benign, dual-use, and malicious-while keeping the underlying task constant. This approach reveals whether models can appropriately calibrate their assistance based on intent rather than simply appearing safe on average. The study found that many models fail to maintain safety across different intent variants, exhibit brittle behavior when prompts are paraphrased, and do not consistently provide safe responses on risky topics.

item.title: Researchers introduce SPLIT benchmark to evaluate empathy and cultural grounding in English and Ukrainian LLM responses, finding performance drops in some models and weak human-AI evaluator agreement [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SPLIT, a 500-prompt benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' (LLMs) ability to generate emotionally grounded responses in English and Ukrainian across five categories related to crisis situations. The study assessed three diverse LLMs on empathetic accuracy, linguistic naturalness, and cultural grounding, revealing that some models' performance declined when switching to Ukrainian, while others remained stable. Additionally, the research found weak agreement between human and AI evaluators on empathy and naturalness, with greater divergence on cultural grounding, highlighting that producing text in Ukrainian does not necessarily equate to providing culturally appropriate emotional support. The SPLIT benchmark aims to fill a gap in evaluating LLMs' cross-lingual empathy and cultural sensitivity, especially in low-to-mid-resource languages during crisis contexts. By comparing model responses in English and Ukrainian, the study underscores the challenges of maintaining empathetic and culturally grounded communication across languages. The findings suggest the need for more culturally tailored benchmarks and emphasize the importance of human-centered evaluation methods to better assess emotional support capabilities in multilingual AI systems.

item.title: Researchers propose Structure-Aware Stratified Partitioning and Curriculum Distributionally Robust Optimization to improve AI evaluation and training in spatially correlated domains, reducing data leakage and hidden stratification [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified that the common assumption of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data splits in AI performance evaluation often fails in spatially and temporally correlated domains such as aerial surveillance, precision agriculture, and medical imaging. This failure leads to data leakage, where correlated samples appear in both training and validation sets, inflating performance metrics, and hidden stratification, where errors in minority subpopulations are masked by overall metrics. To address these challenges, the researchers propose a unified framework combining Structure-Aware Stratified Partitioning (SASP) to create validation splits that minimize leakage while maintaining class balance, and Curriculum Distributionally Robust Optimization (CDRO), a training method that stabilizes optimization under these stricter splits. Testing across multiple benchmarks shows that this approach improves generalization, provides more reliable confidence calibration, and reveals failure modes that traditional random-split evaluations fail to detect. This work offers a significant advancement in evaluating and training AI systems in spatially correlated settings, enhancing the reliability and robustness of their performance assessments.

item.title: Researchers propose SA-HGNN, a Sample-Adaptive Hyperbolic Graph Neural Network model for EEG-based depression recognition capturing hierarchical brain network structures and reducing noise [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new model called Sample-Adaptive Hyperbolic Graph Neural Network (SA-HGNN) to improve EEG-based depression recognition by accurately capturing the hierarchical structure of brain networks affected by depression. The model features three key components: a Sample-Adaptive Graph Construction module that creates personalized brain network topologies, hyperbolic graph convolution to better represent latent hierarchical relationships, and an Attention Pooling module that reduces noise in EEG signals. Experiments on public EEG datasets demonstrate that SA-HGNN outperforms existing methods in both resting-state and task-related scenarios, showing robustness to noise and effectiveness in identifying abnormal brain connectivity patterns associated with depression.

item.title: Researchers present kNNGuard, a training-free LLM guardrail using hidden activations and multi-layer kNN for faster, configurable safety classification across six domains [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced kNNGuard, a training-free guardrail system for large language models (LLMs) that detects unsafe, off-topic, or adversarial prompts by leveraging hidden activations from an off-the-shelf LLM. Using a small labeled bank of 50 safe and unsafe prompts, kNNGuard applies multi-layer k-nearest neighbors (kNN) classification combining activation-space and embedding-space scores. It achieves competitive or superior performance compared to fine-tuned state-of-the-art guardrails across six domains while operating significantly faster, with up to 10 times speed improvement over fine-tuned classifiers. kNNGuard requires no gradient updates or fine-tuning, and domain adaptation is simplified to updating the labeled prompt bank, which can be constructed in under 10 seconds. The study also explores the effects of system prompts, layer selection, and integration into production LLM pipelines, highlighting kNNGuard as a configurable, low-latency safety mechanism suitable for diverse applications.

item.title: Researchers propose Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART) and ART-RL for continuous-time control and reinforcement learning to improve timestep allocation in diffusion sampling, enhancing sample quality and generalization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), a continuous-time control method designed to optimize timestep allocation in score-based diffusion sampling. ART treats the speed of the sampling clock as a control variable, enabling adaptive timesteps that improve sample quality compared to traditional uniform or fixed schedules. To implement this, they developed ART-RL, a reinforcement learning approach that learns optimal timestep schedules through Gaussian policies, effectively turning schedule learning into a continuous-time control problem. The team demonstrated that ART-RL's randomized formulation is equivalent to ART at the optimization level, with its optimal policy recovering the best time-warping rate. Experiments across various settings, including image generation, showed that ART-RL can be integrated into existing diffusion samplers by adjusting only the timestep grid, consistently enhancing sample quality without altering other components. Additionally, the learned schedules generalize well across different sampling budgets, datasets, solvers, and pipelines, indicating broad applicability and robustness.

item.title: Researchers develop deep neural network and ensemble machine learning models to predict early-stage Alzheimer's disease and identify key biomarkers using ADNI data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed machine learning models, including a deep neural network and an ensemble of classifiers, to predict early-stage Alzheimer's disease and identify key biomarkers using data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). The study addresses challenges such as missing data and class imbalance by applying iterative imputation and Borderline SVM-SMOTE, respectively, and uses feature selection methods to focus on important predictors. The models' performance was evaluated using metrics like precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC to determine the most effective approach for early diagnosis. The research integrates clinical details, neuropsychological test scores, and neuroimaging measures to improve detection accuracy. By comparing multiple machine learning techniques, including Logistic Regression, Extra Trees, Bagging KNN, LightGBM, and an artificial neural network, the study aims to enhance early identification of Alzheimer's disease, which is crucial since early symptoms often resemble normal aging and current treatments are limited. Identifying significant biomarkers could support better management and timely intervention for patients.

item.title: Researchers propose Dynamic Neural Graph Encoder to capture sequential inference in neural network weight spaces, improving INR classification accuracy by 10% on CIFAR-100-INR [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Dynamic Neural Graph Encoder (DNG-Encoder), a novel method that represents neural network parameters as dynamic graphs to capture the sequential, layer-by-layer inference process in neural networks. This approach addresses challenges in analyzing high-dimensional weight spaces by preserving the temporal dynamics of neural processing. Using DNG-Encoder, they developed INR2JLS, a framework for downstream tasks such as classifying Implicit Neural Representations (INRs), achieving a roughly 10% improvement in classification accuracy on the CIFAR-100-INR dataset compared to previous methods. The DNG-Encoder's ability to model the sequential nature of neural inference distinguishes it from existing techniques that often overlook this aspect. By encoding the temporal progression of neural network layers, the method enhances the analysis and processing of weight spaces, which are typically complex and high-dimensional. This advancement demonstrates significant performance gains across multiple tasks involving implicit neural representations.

item.title: Researchers analyze challenges of using LLMs as judges in multilingual and low-resource language settings, finding inconsistent evaluations and overreliance on single models, and offer recommendations for NLP community [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have examined the challenges of using large language models (LLMs) as evaluators, or "judges," in multilingual and low-resource language contexts. Their analysis of 650 ACL Anthology papers revealed that only a small fraction focus on these settings, and among those, evaluations often show inconsistent results, an overreliance on single LLMs, and insufficient human validation. The study highlights the limitations of LLMs in less-resourced languages and the risks of overtrusting their judgments in diverse linguistic environments. The researchers provide detailed insights into current practices and emphasize the need for more robust evaluation methods when applying LLMs as judges beyond English. They conclude with recommendations aimed at guiding the natural language processing community to improve the reliability and fairness of LLM-based evaluations in multilingual and low-resource scenarios.

item.title: Researchers find that in offline reinforcement learning, the structure of pessimism impacts generalization more than its amount, with symmetric value functions improving outcomes in contextual MDPs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that in offline reinforcement learning (RL), the structure of pessimism in value functions plays a more critical role in generalization than the degree of pessimism itself. Their study shows that a symmetric, overly pessimistic value function can generalize better in contextual Markov decision processes (CMDPs) than a mildly pessimistic but non-symmetric one. This challenges the notion that excessive conservatism inherently limits generalization. The team explains that the structure of pessimism is influenced by the dataset coverage and that enforcing symmetry in value functions may require techniques like data augmentation (DA). They propose applying DA through a consistency loss during policy extraction rather than traditional offline training on augmented datasets. Their theoretical insights were empirically validated using IQL and CQL algorithms in a rotationally symmetric reacher environment, demonstrating improved generalization outcomes.

item.title: Researchers propose Self-Gating Attention to reduce time and memory complexity in transformer-based time series forecasting, improving inference efficiency on nine real-world datasets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Self-Gating Attention (SGA), a new attention mechanism designed to improve the efficiency of transformer-based time series forecasting. SGA reduces the time and memory complexity from quadratic to linear by using a shared learnable matrix combined with an input-dependent residual component, avoiding the costly query and key projections typical in standard self-attention. This approach addresses redundancy in attention patterns observed in many real-world time series data. The team integrated SGA into various forecasting models and tested it on nine diverse real-world datasets, including electricity, finance, weather, and medical monitoring. Results demonstrated that SGA enhances inference speed and memory usage while maintaining competitive forecasting accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art attention methods. These findings suggest SGA offers a practical solution for resource-constrained or high-throughput forecasting applications.

item.title: Researchers propose SkillFuzz, an execution-free fuzzing approach using contract-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search to detect over 1,000 implicit intents in open skill marketplaces for LLM-based agents [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SkillFuzz, a novel execution-free fuzzing method designed to detect implicit intents arising from the interaction of skills in open marketplaces for Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents. These agents use reusable skills guided by natural-language instructions to automate software engineering tasks, but when skills are combined, they may unintentionally redirect the agent toward undesired objectives. SkillFuzz addresses this challenge by treating implicit-intent discovery as a fuzzing problem over skill compositions, using structured skill contracts and contract-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search to efficiently identify potentially conflicting skill interactions without requiring execution environments. In testing across representative skill-marketplace workloads, SkillFuzz discovered over 1,000 distinct implicit intents within a fixed query budget and confirmed more than 80% of the highest-risk flagged compositions during execution-time validation. The approach outperformed alternative search strategies by identifying significantly more high-severity implicit intents while exploring only a fraction of the possible pairwise skill interactions, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving the safety and reliability of skill marketplaces for LLM-based agents.

item.title: Researchers propose bounded old-state modulation for Self-Modulating Quantum Fast-Weight Programmers to stabilize long-sequence quantum sequence modeling and improve robustness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a bounded old-state modulation technique for Self-Modulating Quantum Fast-Weight Programmers (QFWPs) to enhance stability and robustness in long-sequence quantum sequence modeling. QFWPs store temporal information in variational-circuit parameters, and the self-modulating variant uses input-dependent gates for updating fast weights, but its unbounded old-state multiplier can cause divergence over long sequences. The proposed method applies a bounded, sign-preserving tanh gate to the recurrent memory branch, preventing divergence while maintaining update mechanisms. The team evaluated this approach on quantum-dynamics forecasting tasks and telecommunication activity prediction, finding that old-state modulation consistently improves performance over standard QFWPs. Bounding the old-state gate eliminated long-sequence divergence and enhanced overall robustness. These results highlight accumulated-memory modulation as the key factor in self-modulating QFWPs and demonstrate that bounded gating is an effective stabilization strategy for quantum sequence models.

item.title: Researchers find LLM personas have dual components: frame-robust aggregated traits and frame-dependent geometric features, based on GPT-4o psychometric analysis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed large language model (LLM) personas using psychometric questionnaires and found that persona expression consists of two distinct components: frame-robust aggregated traits, such as Big Five personality scores, and frame-dependent geometric features captured by correlation structures. By manipulating question orderings in GPT-4o simulations of American and Chinese-American personas, they observed that aggregated traits remain relatively stable despite randomization, while geometric features collapse under frame misalignment but recover significantly when frames align. This study reveals that persona geometry is not an intrinsic property but depends on the framing of questions, encoding information beyond what aggregate scores capture. The findings propose a dual-nature framework for evaluating LLM personas, emphasizing the need for frame-aware assessments and challenging traditional views of static personality traits.

item.title: Researchers propose literary analysis frameworks to develop culturally literate AI addressing global textuality, monolingualism, and untranslatability in large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a framework that integrates literary analysis methods to enhance the cultural literacy of large language models (LLMs). The study highlights how LLMs represent a new, large-scale, automated, and predominantly monolingual form of cultural interaction, and argues that tools from literary disciplines-such as comparative literature, narratology, critical theory, and translation studies-are essential for developing AI that can interpret texts with greater nuance and cultural awareness. The framework connects contemporary debates in critical theory with the challenges of structural monolingualism in AI, and suggests applying world literature approaches to address issues of global textuality, including macrostructure, circulation, and untranslatability. This interdisciplinary approach aims to foster pluralistic interpretations and more sophisticated textual models in AI, bridging the gap between literary scholarship and AI development.

item.title: Researchers propose NeuFS, a neuron-aware active few-shot learning framework for LLMs that uses internal neuron activation patterns to improve sample selection and outperform existing methods on reasoning and text classification tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced NeuFS, a neuron-aware active few-shot learning framework designed to enhance large language models (LLMs) by leveraging internal neuron activation patterns for selecting valuable unlabeled samples. Unlike traditional methods that rely on output-level signals such as predictive entropy or semantic similarity, NeuFS focuses on the models' internal dynamics to identify diverse and informative samples, particularly those prone to hallucination. This approach aims to reduce human annotation costs while improving performance in specialized domains. NeuFS employs a dual-criteria selection strategy that ensures sample diversity through neuron pattern coverage and prioritizes challenging examples by measuring neuron consensus. Experiments across three datasets demonstrate that NeuFS outperforms existing active few-shot learning baselines in reasoning and text classification tasks. Further analysis confirms that internal neuron activations provide a more effective and principled signal for sample selection compared to external embeddings, highlighting the framework's potential to advance few-shot learning techniques for LLMs.

item.title: Researchers propose QFedAgent, a quantum-classical personalized federated learning framework for multi-agent activity recognition achieving 97.7% accuracy with 10x parameter reduction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed QFedAgent, a hybrid quantum-classical personalized federated learning framework designed for multi-agent activity recognition. This approach addresses challenges in federated learning caused by heterogeneous, non-independent, and non-identically distributed multimodal sensor data in multi-agent systems. By integrating a variational quantum circuit fusion module, QFedAgent models interactions between accelerometer and gyroscope data using quantum state encoding and entanglement, significantly reducing the number of parameters required compared to classical methods. The quantum fusion module uses only 72 quantum rotation parameters, compared to 33,000 parameters in traditional multi-layer perceptron-based fusion, achieving about a tenfold reduction in total parameters. Experiments on the OPPORTUNITY dataset with subject-based non-IID partitions demonstrated that QFedAgent achieves a mean test accuracy of 97.7%, showing that quantum-enhanced fusion can maintain competitive performance while improving parameter efficiency in federated learning for robotic sensing applications.

item.title: Researchers propose Neuron On-Policy Self-Distillation framework using neuron activations for annotation-free LLM training, improving in-domain performance and cross-domain generalization in specialized domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Neuron On-Policy Self-Distillation (Neuron-OPSD), a novel framework for training large language models (LLMs) without relying on human-labeled data or real-world interaction feedback. This approach uses internal neuron activations to guide the selection of training data and the construction of teacher contexts, enabling on-policy distillation from the teacher distribution without any ground-truth labels. Neuron-OPSD aims to improve performance in specialized domains while maintaining generalization across different domains and reducing calibration errors seen in previous annotation-free methods. The framework addresses challenges in post-training LLM adaptation where expert annotations are costly or unavailable, particularly in specialized fields. Unlike prior methods that suffer from out-of-domain performance degradation or inflated calibration errors, Neuron-OPSD leverages a data-centric strategy that enhances in-domain task accuracy and preserves cross-domain robustness. This method is especially relevant for scenarios where online interaction or external supervision is impractical, distinguishing itself from offline reinforcement learning approaches that depend on logged, reward-labeled data.

item.title: Researchers present OrbitQuant, a data-agnostic quantizer for image and video diffusion transformers that enables post-training quantization without per-modality tuning and achieves state-of-the-art results at low-bit settings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed OrbitQuant, a novel data-agnostic quantizer designed for image and video diffusion transformers (DiTs) that enables efficient post-training quantization without the need for per-modality tuning. OrbitQuant uses a normalized, rotated basis with a randomized permuted block-Hadamard rotation to stabilize activation distributions across different timesteps, prompts, and layers, allowing a single quantization codebook to be applied universally. This approach reduces inference costs while maintaining high-quality generation. The method extends to weight quantization by integrating the rotation into the weights, which cancels out during computation, leaving only a forward rotation on activations at runtime. OrbitQuant has demonstrated state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, including FLUX.1, Z-Image-Turbo, Wan 2.1, and CogVideoX, achieving effective low-bit quantization and advancing the practical use of PTQ for image diffusion transformers to configurations like W2A4 with usable generation quality.

item.title: Researchers introduce TestEvo-Bench, a live benchmark for test and code co-evolution with 1,255 tasks from 152 Java projects, evaluating AI agents on test generation and update success rates [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TestEvo-Bench, a live benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on the co-evolution of software tests and code. The benchmark includes 1,255 tasks from 152 open-source Java projects, divided into two tracks: test generation, where agents create new tests to reflect updated software behavior, and test update, where agents modify existing tests to align with code changes. Each task is linked to real commit histories and supports execution-based metrics such as pass rate and coverage, enabling a more accurate assessment of an agent's understanding of code-test relationships. TestEvo-Bench continuously updates with new tasks mined from software repositories, allowing evaluations to focus on data beyond a model's training period to minimize data leakage. Experiments with four state-of-the-art AI agents combining advanced harnesses and foundation models showed success rates up to 77.5% for test generation and 74.6% for test updates. However, performance declines on the most recent tasks and under constraints limiting computational resources per task, highlighting ongoing challenges in automated test maintenance.

item.title: Researchers compare SOAP, Muon, and hybrid optimizers to Adam for training machine learning interatomic potentials, finding faster convergence and higher accuracy especially under partial force supervision [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have evaluated new matrix-structured optimizers-Muon, SOAP, and a hybrid SOAP-Muon-against the commonly used Adam optimizer for training machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Their study shows that these alternative optimizers, particularly SOAP and SOAP-Muon, achieve faster convergence and higher accuracy when training NequIP and Allegro MLIP models, especially under conditions of partial force supervision. Muon provides some improvement but is less effective than the other two. The findings highlight that while much focus has been on model architectures and datasets, the choice of optimizer has been largely overlooked in MLIP training. This research suggests that selecting the right optimizer can significantly enhance training efficiency and model performance, marking an important consideration for future MLIP development.

item.title: Researchers introduce DemoPSD, a self-distillation framework that mitigates privileged information leakage and preserves exploration in large language model training, outperforming prior methods on scientific benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed DemoPSD, a new self-distillation framework designed to improve the training of large language models (LLMs) by addressing the issue of privileged information leakage and preserving exploration during learning. DemoPSD selectively blends teacher and student model outputs using a reverse-KL barycenter target, which balances guidance from the teacher with the student's own reasoning capabilities. This approach mitigates overfitting to in-domain data and prevents the student model from relying on shortcuts unavailable during testing. The framework adaptively adjusts the influence of the teacher at each token position based on the discrepancy between teacher and student distributions. Experiments on scientific benchmarks across multiple fields demonstrate that DemoPSD outperforms existing methods like GRPO and SDPO, maintaining higher training entropy and showing robust generalization to out-of-distribution tasks. The method offers a promising direction for enhancing LLM reasoning and cross-domain performance while reducing reliance on privileged information.

item.title: Researchers introduce DramaSR-LRM, a reasoning large language model that improves speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas using multimodal context on a 532K dialogue benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed DramaSR-LRM, a large reasoning language model designed to improve speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas by integrating auditory, linguistic, and visual information. This approach addresses the challenge of accurately attributing spoken lines to characters, which is crucial for understanding complex storylines. The team also introduced DramaSR-532K, a large-scale benchmark dataset with 532,000 annotated dialogue lines from over 900 characters, to support this task. DramaSR-LRM autonomously combines multimodal contextual evidence to enhance attribution accuracy, particularly excelling in cases with short utterances where traditional acoustic methods struggle. Experimental results show that this model significantly outperforms existing baselines. The researchers plan to make all data and code publicly available to facilitate further research in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose MAGIK framework enabling reinforcement learning agents to transfer knowledge to analogous tasks via imagination-based analogy mapping without target environment interaction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MAGIK, a new framework designed to enable reinforcement learning (RL) agents to transfer knowledge to similar tasks without needing to interact with the new environment. MAGIK uses an imagination-based mechanism to map elements of a target task to their counterparts in a previously learned source task, allowing the agent to apply its existing policy directly. This approach addresses the common challenge in RL where agents require extensive retraining even for structurally related tasks.
