This method uses Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) reinforcement learning combined with deep audio steganography to embed sample-specific triggers into audio data, enabling the attack to bypass many existing defenses without altering labels. The approach optimizes target samples in the model's latent space to create effective backdoor triggers that cause misclassification during inference. Tests on three datasets and four different deep neural networks show that DRL-CLBA achieves a high success rate and resists common defense techniques such as fine-tuning, pruning, and spectral signature detection. This exposes significant vulnerabilities in speech-controlled systems and highlights the need for improved security measures against sophisticated backdoor attacks in audio-based AI applications.

item.title: Researchers report three reformalizations of the Jordan Curve Theorem across Mizar, Lean, HOL Light, and Agda proof assistants, analyzing pipeline design choices for practical tasks
item.description: Researchers have conducted a case study on reformalization, a process where formal proofs developed in one proof assistant are translated into another. They report three reformalizations of the Jordan Curve Theorem, transferring proofs from Mizar to Lean, from HOL Light to Lean, and from HOL Light to Agda. The study examines the outcomes and highlights key pipeline design decisions that influence the effectiveness of practical reformalization tasks. This work provides insights into the challenges and considerations involved in adapting formal proofs across different proof assistant systems, contributing to the broader effort of improving interoperability and automation in formal verification.

item.title: Researchers present a meta-benchmarking framework organizing 452 financial-services LLM benchmarks into 38 banking domains, evaluating 288 models from 25 organizations as of June 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a meta-benchmarking framework that organizes 452 publicly reported benchmarks related to financial services into 38 banking business domains, covering areas such as sales, operations, risk, and support. This framework evaluates 288 large language models from 25 organizations as of June 2026, addressing the limitations of existing leaderboards that focus on global average performance and often overlook the specific cognitive demands of financial services tasks. The framework uses a multiplicative weighting scheme based on discrimination, coverage, and recency to prioritize benchmarks that effectively differentiate top models, are widely used, and remain relevant. These weights inform a pairwise Elo tournament system to produce comparable scores across benchmarks without raw score normalization. The researchers provide detailed methodology, taxonomy, and design considerations to support reproducibility and assist institutions in model selection and governance challenges within the financial sector.

item.title: Researchers introduce Phi-Nav, a hindsight reasoning framework for Vision-Language Navigation that aligns instructions with exploratory trajectories to improve training efficiency on R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Phi-Nav, a new framework for Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) that improves training efficiency by aligning language instructions with the agent's actual exploratory paths. Phi-Nav uses a three-stage process involving oracle-guided exploration, synthesis of hindsight instructions based on visual observations, and a second imitation learning phase with these synthesized instructions. This approach addresses the semantic mismatch between executed trajectories and original instructions common in on-policy exploration. Evaluations on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks demonstrate that Phi-Nav achieves competitive performance while requiring significantly fewer expert demonstrations compared to existing methods. By converting unlabeled exploratory movements into meaningful training signals, Phi-Nav enhances semantic exploration in VLN and offers an effective solution for training embodied agents with limited data.

item.title: Researchers present Mastermind, a dual-loop framework that learns transferable strategies for repository-scale vulnerability reproduction, achieving up to 84.5% pass rate with GPT-5.5 executor on CyberGym tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Mastermind, a dual-loop framework designed to improve repository-scale vulnerability reproduction in software engineering. Mastermind focuses on learning transferable high-level strategies rather than full action sequences, enabling an agent to inspect codebases, infer input grammars, construct proof-of-concept exploits, and verify fixes more effectively. The framework separates strategy learning from task-specific experience, allowing a trainable planner to guide multiple executors without altering their action capabilities. Evaluated on the CyberGym benchmark with 260 training and 200 evaluation tasks, Mastermind achieved an 84.5% success rate using GPT-5.5 as the executor, outperforming previous methods such as open-book proof-of-concept context and iterative improvement. The same planner also enhanced the performance of GPT-5.4 mini and GLM 5.1 models, demonstrating that learning reusable strategies can significantly boost the effectiveness of software engineering agents across different executors.

item.title: Researchers present SimWorlds, a multi-agent system generating dynamic, editable 4D scenes from text with Blender integration and introduce 4DBuildBench benchmark for visual and physical fidelity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SimWorlds, a multi-agent system that generates dynamic, editable 4D scenes from text inputs, integrating procedural knowledge specific to Blender. Unlike previous systems that produce static 3D scenes, SimWorlds coordinates spatial layout, physics solvers, temporal sequencing, camera, and lighting to create coherent scenes featuring moving liquids, particles, and mechanisms. The system employs a planner-coder-reviewer workflow, a layered scene protocol with deterministic verification, and runtime inspection tools to detect issues not visible in rendered images. Alongside SimWorlds, the team introduced 4DBuildBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate both the visual fidelity and physical consistency of procedurally generated dynamic 3D scenes from text prompts. Experimental results demonstrate that SimWorlds outperforms existing dynamic Blender generation methods, advancing the creation of physics-grounded, editable content useful for video generation and embodied AI applications.

item.title: Researchers propose WM-SAR method to repair agent planning graphs by targeting error-amplifying subgraphs, outperforming traditional LLM correctors under realistic token budgets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new method called WM-SAR (World-Model Subgraph Amplification Repair) to improve the correction of large agent planning graphs, which often contain thousands of steps and are prone to failures. Unlike traditional approaches that scan for visible errors and attempt local repairs, WM-SAR identifies and targets the subgraphs responsible for amplifying errors, sending only these causal regions to a language model for repair. This approach significantly outperforms existing engineering correctors, especially under realistic token budget constraints, achieving near-complete stabilization of the planning graph with a more focused and efficient repair process. The study highlights the limitations of full-graph replanning, which is computationally expensive and can overwhelm language models with irrelevant information. By working backward from error amplification rather than symptoms, WM-SAR provides a cleaner and more effective repair target. Experiments with graph simulations and language model repairs demonstrate that WM-SAR maintains stability across large planning workflows while using fewer computational resources, marking a notable advancement in persistent agent planning systems.

item.title: Researchers propose retrieval-augmented small language model with formal concept analysis for verifiable knowledge expansion, demonstrating results on rare ataxia data from Orphadata [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a retrieval-augmented small language model (SLM) framework that integrates formal concept analysis (FCA) to verify and expand knowledge in ontology construction. This approach uses FCA to propose implications based on seed attributes, which are then validated or refuted by a retrieval-grounded SLM oracle, allowing for inspection of accepted implications, counterexamples, and corrections. The method was tested on rare ataxia data from Orphadata, achieving relation F1 scores between 0.29 and 0.52 and implication F1 scores between 0.22 and 0.30, with larger seed sets improving performance. The framework supports incidence judgments, consistency checks, and attribute proposals, enhancing the reliability of knowledge expansion. Despite improvements, identifying positive object-attribute pairs remains challenging even when candidate objects and attributes are fixed. The study highlights the potential of combining symbolic verification with language models to produce more verifiable and consistent ontological knowledge.

item.title: Researchers present Vera, an automated safety testing framework for LLM agents that discovers risks, runs executable safety cases, and verifies outcomes with evidence, revealing high attack success rates across four agent frameworks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Vera, an automated safety testing framework designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents that perform autonomous actions using external tools. Vera employs a three-stage process that discovers emerging safety risks, generates executable safety cases, and verifies outcomes based on observable evidence rather than model self-reporting. This approach addresses the limitations of existing safety tests, which rely on expert-designed violations and hard-coded evaluation rules, making them less adaptable to evolving agents. The framework was tested on four production agent platforms-OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, and Claude Code-revealing significant safety vulnerabilities with attack success rates averaging 93.9% under multi-channel attacks. Vera also includes Vera-Bench, a comprehensive suite of 1,600 executable safety cases covering 124 risk categories across various execution environments. The researchers emphasize that modular, executable testing infrastructure like Vera is crucial for maintaining rigorous and scalable safety evaluations as agentic systems continue to evolve rapidly. The Vera codebase is publicly available for further use and development.

item.title: Researchers introduce MMIR-TCM, a multimodal AI framework integrating memory-augmented segmentation and retrieval-augmented generation for Traditional Chinese Medicine diagnosis, validated on a new large-scale dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MMIR-TCM, a multimodal AI framework designed to improve Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis by integrating memory-augmented segmentation and retrieval-augmented generation. This system mimics expert diagnostic processes by combining a training-free tongue extraction module, a fine-tuned model for structured diagnosis, and an evidence-based clinical decision support component. The framework was validated using MedTCM, a newly introduced large-scale multimodal dataset for TCM research, and evaluated with a novel domain-specific metric that captures clinical accuracy more effectively than existing measures. MMIR-TCM addresses key challenges in TCM diagnosis, such as subjectivity and the semantic gap between visual tongue features and textual reasoning, which have hindered the application of AI in this field. The three-stage architecture includes a Memory-SAM module for robust tongue segmentation, a Qwen3-VL model for diagnosis generation, and a Qwen3-based retrieval-augmented generation system for clinical support. Experimental results show that MMIR-TCM outperforms leading AI models like GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash, demonstrating its potential to enhance the accuracy and reproducibility of TCM clinical tasks.

item.title: Researchers apply Halpern & Pearl's actual causality theory to fault trees, classifying causality notions and linking minimal cut sets to actual causes for failure diagnostics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have applied Halpern and Pearl's theory of actual causality to fault trees, which are commonly used risk models for complex systems. This approach enables fault trees to address not only what can go wrong but also why failures occur, enhancing failure diagnostics. The study provides a comprehensive classification of different notions of actual causality based on the fault tree's graph and logical structures, demonstrating how minimal cut sets correspond to actual causes of system failures. By linking minimal cut sets to actual causes, the research offers a deeper understanding of failure mechanisms within complex systems. This connection allows for more precise identification of causal factors in fault trees, which traditionally focus on potential failure scenarios. The findings contribute to improving diagnostic methods by clarifying the causal relationships underlying system faults.

item.title: Researchers present CLAP, a closed-loop method for domain agent post-training that integrates data validation, evaluation, and release control to manage adapter suitability and reduce risks in manufacturing scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CLAP (Closed-Loop Agent Post-training), a method designed to improve the post-training process of domain agents by integrating data validation, evaluation, and release control. CLAP transforms business data into structured samples and diagnostic records, enabling a comprehensive assessment of adapter suitability for specific application chains. Testing on manufacturing scenarios showed modest improvements in performance metrics, though results varied across batches, highlighting risks such as high KL divergence. The approach combines multiple techniques including reward and KL diagnosis, offline gating, and application-chain replay to manage the complexities of noisy data and uncertain training outcomes. Notably, application-chain replay demonstrated the necessity of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for accurate factual extraction, with RAG-oriented adapters improving key performance indicators despite increased latency. These findings suggest that managing domain-agent post-training through an integrated loop of data processing, training, evaluation, and controlled release is more effective than relying solely on training completion or single offline scores. This approach aims to reduce risks and enhance the reliability of domain-specific AI agents in practical manufacturing environments.

item.title: Researchers introduce CamoNAS, a frequency-aware neural architecture search framework for camouflaged object detection achieving state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CamoNAS, a frequency-aware neural architecture search framework designed to improve camouflaged object detection (COD). This approach automatically optimizes both cell-level operations and network-level downsampling paths within a hierarchical search space, enhancing the detection of objects that blend into their surroundings. CamoNAS incorporates an RGB frequency dual-stream architecture, combining a learnable wavelet transform with the traditional RGB spatial stream to better capture subtle features. CamoNAS outperforms existing methods on four major COD benchmarks-CAMO, COD10K, NC4K, and CHAMELEON-demonstrating the effectiveness of neural architecture search in this challenging domain. The framework addresses limitations of prior models that relied on hand-designed architectures and intuition-based multi-scale feature fusion. The researchers have made their code publicly available to support further development in camouflaged object detection.
